label_spreading_blocked

Source: R/label_propagation.R
label_spreading_blocked.Rd

Memory-efficient label spreading (blocked, HDF5 optional) Runs label spreading on a sparse graph in **class blocks** to control memory, optionally streaming class probabilities to an on-disk HDF5 dataset.

Usage

label_spreading_blocked(
  adj,
  labels,
  label_n = NULL,
  alpha = 0.9,
  max_iter = 100,
  tol = 0.001,
  block_size = 128,
  outfile = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  epsilon = 0
)

Arguments

adj

dgCMatrix sparse adjacency; will be row-normalized in-place to act as a transition matrix.

labels

Integer or numeric vector of length \(N\) with class labels in 1..C and NA for unlabeled cells. Do not refactor.

label_n

Optional total number of classes; inferred if NULL.

alpha

Damping parameter in label propagation update.

max_iter

Maximum iterations per block.

tol

Convergence tolerance for updates.

block_size

Number of classes per block to process at once.

outfile

Optional HDF5 file path; if NULL, returns dense matrix.

verbose

Logical; show progress messages.

epsilon

Small uniform prior mass per class to avoid zeros.

Value

If outfile = NULL, a dense \(N \times C\) numeric matrix of class probabilities. Otherwise, invisibly returns the HDF5 file path with dataset "prob" written.

Details

- Normalizes the adjacency to a row-stochastic matrix. - Splits the label space into block_size-sized groups to limit RAM use. - Optionally writes each probability block directly into an HDF5 dataset.

See also

create_hdf5_matrix, normalize_hdf5_rows, label_spreading_bootstrap_blocked

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(Matrix)
set.seed(1)
N <- 1000; C <- 5
A <- rsparsematrix(N, N, 0.001); A <- abs(A) + Diagonal(N)
labs <- sample(c(1:C, NA), N, TRUE, prob = c(rep(0.05, C), 0.75))
P <- label_spreading_blocked(A, labs, label_n = C, block_size = 2, max_iter = 50)
} # }
